intro: Seattle rewards visitors with a walkable waterfront, world-class coffee, and easy escapes to water and mountains. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Link light rail 1 Line links Sea-Tac, Downtown, Capitol Hill, and the University of Washington.
King County Metro buses cover the city; ORCA card or phone tap pays fares.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft both operate widely.
Driving is easy to arrange but Downtown traffic is heavy at most hours.
Walking is good Downtown and on the waterfront; bikes and e-scooters are common.
Washington State Ferries leave Downtown for Bainbridge Island and Bremerton.

space-needle.name: Space Needle
space-needle.price_text: ≈ $35–45 adult; cheaper for kids and seniors — check on the day
space-needle.tip: Go early morning or near sunset for the clearest views. Book a timed ticket online to skip the line.

pike-place.name: Pike Place Market
pike-place.hours: Most stalls about 09:00–18:00; some restaurants later
pike-place.tip: Come before 10:00 to see the fish throwers without the crowds. Bring cash for small stalls.

chihuly.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
chihuly.tip: The glasshouse and garden look best in daylight. Combine with the Space Needle for a discount.

mopop.name: Museum of Pop Culture
mopop.tip: Allow two hours. The horror and sci-fi exhibits are the highlights for many visitors.

aquarium.name: Seattle Aquarium
aquarium.tip: Good for families and rainy days. Book online; entry times can sell out.

argosy-cruise.name: Argosy Harbor Cruise
argosy-cruise.tip: Sit on the open deck for skyline photos. Bring a jacket; it is windy on the water.

lumen-field.name: Lumen Field
lumen-field.price_text: Tour or match ticket price varies — check on the day
lumen-field.hours: Event days only; tours on select days
lumen-field.tip: Check the schedule before you go. Match days are loud and fun — arrive early.

playtime-fun.name: Playtime Family Fun
playtime-fun.price_text: ≈ $12–20 per child — check on the day
playtime-fun.tip: Good rainy-day stop for younger kids. Confirm hours before you go.

central-library.name: Seattle Central Library
central-library.tip: Ride the escalators to the top floor for the view. The red hall is a great photo stop.

starbucks.name: Starbucks (original store)
starbucks.tip: Expect a line at the first store in Pike Place. The queue moves fast.

reserve-roastery.name: Starbucks Reserve Roastery Seattle
reserve-roastery.tip: More relaxed than the original store. Try a small-batch coffee and watch the roasting.

suzzallo.name: Suzzallo Library
suzzallo.tip: See the grand reading room on the third floor. Be quiet — students are studying.

uw.name: University of Washington
uw.tip: Walk the Quad in spring for cherry blossoms. The view from Rainier Vista is worth the stroll.

wild-waves.name: Wild Waves Theme Park
wild-waves.tip: It is a drive south of the city. Check the calendar — it is mostly a summer park.

woodland-zoo.name: Woodland Park Zoo
woodland-zoo.tip: Big park — wear comfortable shoes. Go early to see animals before the heat.

kerry-park.name: Kerry Park viewpoint
kerry-park.tip: The classic skyline photo spot. Come at sunset or blue hour.

gum-wall.name: Gum Wall
gum-wall.tip: Quick stop under Pike Place Market. It is small — pair it with the market visit.

waterfront-park.name: Seattle Waterfront Park walk
waterfront-park.tip: Walk the waterfront promenade between the aquarium and the ferries. Watch for the new overlooks.

underground-tour.name: Bill Speidel's Underground Tour
underground-tour.tip: Funny, history-heavy walk under Pioneer Square. Book ahead on weekends.

discovery-park.name: Discovery Park
discovery-park.tip: Walk to the lighthouse for a quiet beach and water views. Bring layers.

ferry-bainbridge.name: Bainbridge Island ferry ride
ferry-bainbridge.price_text: ≈ $9–10 walk-on round trip — check on the day
ferry-bainbridge.tip: A cheap way to get on the water. Walk on and stroll the town near the dock.

stays.why: Walk to Pike Place, the waterfront and the Space Needle; Link light rail to the airport and University of Washington.
Best food and nightlife on foot; a Link light rail stop and a short ride to Downtown.
Between Downtown and the Space Needle; good bars and restaurants, walkable to the waterfront.
Quieter and modern, near the Space Needle and Lake Union; good for longer stays, less nightlife.

food: Start at Pike Place Market: walk the stalls, watch the fish throwers, and grab a cheap pastry or chowder.
Seattle is a coffee city. Try a local roaster's café rather than a chain; expect about $4–6 for a latte.
Seafood is the local specialty: salmon, crab and oysters. Waterfront and market restaurants cost more; check menus first.
Budget eats: teriyaki, pho and food trucks around Capitol Hill and the University District, often $10–15 a meal.
Book popular dinner spots ahead, especially on weekends. Many kitchens close earlier than in bigger cities.
more_time: Take a Washington State Ferries trip from Downtown to Bainbridge Island: a short crossing with skyline views. Check fares and times on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for a day trip toward the mountains or water; ask your hotel about current options and conditions.
Museum lovers can add the Museum of Pop Culture or the Seattle Art Museum; check opening days and prices before you go.
